```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# Your data: add the file with "Add Data Files…", then read it here instead, e.g.
#   data <- haven::read_sav("my_study.sav") |> haven::as_factor()
data <- read_csv("astronauts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# APA number formatting (from the Dissertation Dock)
fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
fmt_p <- function(p) if (p < .001) "< .001" else paste("=", sub("^0", "", fmt_num(p, 3)))
```

## Participants

The data set holds `r format(nrow(data), big.mark = ",")` rows and `r ncol(data)` variables.

## Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptives
#| echo: false
data |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarise(n = n(), M = mean(hours_mission), SD = sd(hours_mission)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Mission length in hours by sex")
```

## Hypothesis test

```{r}
#| label: test
#| include: false
test <- t.test(hours_mission ~ sex, data = data)
```

Write each result with inline code, never by hand: *t*(`r fmt_num(test$parameter)`) =
`r fmt_num(test$statistic)`, *p* `r fmt_p(test$p.value)`. (This template counts missions, not
people; your own analysis needs one row per participant.)
